content:
Maya (Support): heads up — multiple customers (acct: tilt-ai, sprite-inc) are filing tickets for intermittent 429s starting ~03:10 UTC. they all started after last night's rate-policy push. sample from tilt-ai:

Maya (Support): ```
POST /v1/generate  HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer redacted
X-Org-ID: tilt-ai
Content-Length: 232

Response: 429 Too Many Requests
{ "error": "rate_exceeded", "detail": "quota exhausted for org" }
```

Maya (Support): they say requests were steady historically, small bursts but within previous limits. tickets show no auth errors and no billing alerts.

Ravi (SRE): thanks. which policy exactly was pushed? audit log shows a policy diff at 03:05 UTC by @Jules.

Jules (EngPlatform): yep pushed a staged throughput cap change for server-generated tokens: reduced per-org concurrent tokens from 200 -> 120 and tightened burst window from 60s -> 30s. this was intended for canary group only (10% traffic) but I see the rollout flag may have been mis-targeted. deploy-bot: @deploy-bot pushed policy config `rate-policy-v2` to env=prod at 03:05 UTC.

deploy-bot: [bot] config push: rate-policy-v2 -> prod (canary=10%). change-id: cp-2026-03-15-09

Ravi (SRE): ok that explains 429 spike. can you paste the policy snippet? especially the gating rule.

Jules (EngPlatform): snippet:

Jules (EngPlatform): ```json
{
  "name": "per_org_concurrency",
  "default": 120,
  "burst_window_sec": 30,
  "canary": { "pct": 10, "selector": { "route": "*" } }
}
```

Maya (Support): customers in tickets are not in our canary list. tilt-ai definitely not. they reported errors from multiple regions.

Ravi (SRE): possibility: the canary selector logic used `route: "*"` which accidentally matched internal admin routes and VIP orgs. or rollout targeting key-prefix mismatch. i'm pulling metrics now — gimme 2m.

Sam (Oncall): i'm looking at rate limit cluster metrics. surge in 429s starting 03:07 UTC across rbx/us-east and iad. 95th p99 token latency is fine, redis quotas show a bump in eviction/backpressure around 03:06.

Ravi (SRE): looking at org-level throttle map: tilt-ai and sprite-inc moved from 200->120 concurrent. their queue length spiked. that combined with our auto-burst smoothing caused immediate 429s.

Ari (Product): how do we avoid customer-impact during canaries? we intended to test silently. if selector mis-evaluated, we should rollback immediately and run a postmortem.

Jules (EngPlatform): agree. i can rollback the config. but note the policy is in config store and there's a staged rollout controller; rollback will take ~90s to propagate. do we want full rollback to previous policy or adjust canary selector to be explicit for the test corpus?

Ravi (SRE): emergency mitigation options:
- rollback the push (fast, global)
- apply temporary org-level exception (bypass) for affected orgs (targeted, quick)
- increase default concurrency back to 200 while we fix selector (less safe for long term)

Maya (Support): tilt-ai asked for timeline and a repro they can test; they want no more throttles. they offered to reduce client concurrency but want a fix from our side.

Sam (Oncall): i can apply org bypass for tilt-ai + sprite-inc now — will that suppress 429s?

Ravi (SRE): yes org-bypass will short-circuit policy evaluation and restore previous limits. do it for the affected two orgs as immediate triage. then Jules roll back the config.

Sam (Oncall): applying bypass for orgs: tilt-ai, sprite-inc...

Sam (Oncall): applied. 

Sam (Oncall): quick check: tilt-ai 429s dropped to near zero within one minute. confirming with tickets.

Maya (Support): tilt confirmed no 429s now, thanks. 

Jules (EngPlatform): initiating rollback of `rate-policy-v2` -> restoring `rate-policy-v1`. rollback request sent to controller.

deploy-bot: [bot] rollback started: cp-2026-03-15-09 -> rate-policy-v1. eta ~90s.

Ravi (SRE): good. follow-up actions:
- Jules: audit selector logic. ensure canary selector cannot match `route: "*"` or internal VIPs by default. add negative-match rules for vip orgs.
- EngPlatform & SRE: add pre-deploy integration test that evaluates selector resolution against org metadata list.
- Support: notify affected customers and offer token-level retries/backoff guidance.
- Product: review rollout gating policy and approval steps.

Ari (Product): will set up a quick sync with EngPlatform to adjust rollout docs. also want to add a rollback SLO for policy pushes.

Maya (Support): i'll update tickets: sent apology, explained rollback + org-bypass done, offered one week of overage credit if they want (ok with finance?).

Ravi (SRE): finance approval for small credits is fine — ping finance if >$5k.

Jules (EngPlatform): selector fix: will change canary semantics to explicit org-list or header token and add a dry-run flag that logs matches but doesn't enforce. will push change to staging, then canary 1% for 24h.

Sam (Oncall): rollout rollback complete. deploy-bot shows config hash reverted at 03:09:45 UTC. 429s returned to baseline.

deploy-bot: [bot] rollback complete: cp-2026-03-15-09 -> rate-policy-v1 at 03:09:45 UTC.

Maya (Support): closing loop with tilt-ai: they confirmed normal operation, asked for postmortem. pls add me to the postmortem doc.

Ravi (SRE): will own postmortem. initial blameless notes: canary selector mis-targeting + lack of dry-run + insufficient production pre-checks.

Jules (EngPlatform): will add explicit rollout checklist: target whitelist, dry-run matches, small percentage canary, metric watch thresholds, and an automatic rollback threshold (e.g., >0.5% surge 429s for 5m).

Maya (Support): thanks all. closing thread for now. will reopen if any more regressions. :thumbsup:
